subject: Renewal discussion — Reverie Health: mid-contract uplift, co-term options
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Morris <elaine@reveriehealth.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@reveriehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — Reverie Health: mid-contract uplift, co-term options

Hi Elaine / Contracts team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As discussed, Reverie is expecting a mid-contract capacity increase driven by Q3 product pilots, and you asked for a couple of concrete packaging options we can sign quickly.

Attached: Reverb_Renewal_SOW_v1.pdf (draft SOW) and redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx (base numbers).

Two paths to consider — high level:
- Option 1 (Smoothing): One-time uplift invoiced immediately, with a smoothing credit applied across remaining term to keep monthly OPEX impact lower.
- Option 2 (Staged Top-up + Co-term): Staged top-up: immediate partial top-up for pilot, second tranche at co-term date; pro rata invoicing for partial period. This preserves budget alignment for procurement.

Questions for you: which is more important to procurement — minimizing immediate spend, or simplifying to a single invoice and co-term? If you prefer co-term, we can line up the second tranche to hit co-term and offer a modest onboarding credit.

I’ve cc’d Lauren for handoff and internal pacing. If procurement wants a fully redlined SOW and a single consolidated invoice path, we can turn that around by Friday.

Next steps: Please confirm preferred path and any internal approval windows. If helpful we can schedule a 20-min call tomorrow to walk numbers.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments (referenced): Reverb_Renewal_SOW_v1.pdf (draft SOW), redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Elaine Morris <elaine@reveriehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@reveriehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — Reverie Health: mid-contract uplift, co-term options

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the summary and the materials — appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement is leaning toward minimizing immediate spend because the Q3 pilots are still in the approval stage for some business units. Our priorities:

- Keep near-term cash outlay low (so Option 1 looks attractive)
- Keep contract footprint simple for legal (prefer single amendment vs two invoices if possible)
- Align any uplift with our fiscal calendar; co-terming to 12/31 would be ideal.

Request: can you provide a breakdown that shows (a) immediate invoice amount under Option 1, (b) monthly effective spend after smoothing credit, and (c) a co-term version of Option 2 where the second tranche hits 12/31? Also need an editable SOW (Word) so our legal can redline.

If you can get that by end of day Thursday our procurement lead will review on Friday morning. We can do a quick call Friday if needed.

Best,
Elaine
VP Product & Ops
Reverie Health
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Reverie renewal — procurement asks / numbers needed

Folks — forwarding Reverie procurement note (below). They want three deliverables by EOD Thursday:

1) Immediate invoice amount for Option 1 (one-time uplift + smoothing credit)
2) Effective monthly spend number after smoothing credit (showing net OPEX impact)
3) A co-term variant of Option 2 aligned to 2028-12-31 + editable SOW

My suggestion (draft):
- Option A (Smoothing): $180k one-time uplift today, apply $60k smoothing credit across remaining 6 months -> net monthly increase ~$20k
- Option B (Staged/Co-term): Immediate partial top-up $75k today, second tranche $125k at co-term (12/31). Invoice pro rata for partial month. Offer a 3% onboarding credit on total uplift if they sign co-term by 6/15.

Please weigh in on margin and whether we can stretch the onboarding credit to 5% if they commit to a 12-month renewal at co-term. Olga — can you prepare an editable SOW and flag any legal issues with staged top-up language? Rishi — need a quick P&L on both options and cashflow impact across remaining term.

I’ll stitch together the customer-facing packet once we have numbers.

Thanks,
Ben
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reverie renewal — quick finance take

Ben / Lauren — quick read on the numbers. Assumptions: existing term ends 2028-12-31, remaining months = 6, cost-of-servicing uplift incremental is ~18% of uplift value.

Option A (Smoothing):
- One-time invoice: $180,000
- Smoothing credit applied: $60,000 over 6 months ($10k/month)
- Net monthly increase: $180k/6 - $10k = $20k/month (matches your calc)
- Gross margin on uplift: ~82%

Option B (Staged/Co-term):
- Immediate: $75,000
- Second tranche at co-term (12/31): $125,000
- If we give a 5% onboarding credit on total uplift ($200k): credit = $10k -> net revenue $190k
- Cashflow: Option B brings $75k cash now vs $180k in Option A. From a cash perspective, Option A is better. From a margin/profitability view both similar after credits.

Recommendation: move forward with Option B but with a 3% onboarding credit (we can approve 3% without VP sign-off); reserve 5% as escalation to Sales Leadership only if they sign a minimum 12-month co-term commitment (explicit in SOW).

I’ve attached an updated pricing matrix with line items & calculated monthly impacts (see redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx referenced in Ben’s packet).

Rishi
VP Finance
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Morris <elaine@reveriehealth.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@reveriehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed path — combined option (staged top-up + smoothing guardrails)

Elaine — thanks for the quick feedback and context. Based on procurement priorities and finance guidance, here’s a customer-ready proposal we can sign this week:

Proposed path (preferred): Staged Top-up with Co-term and Small Onboarding Credit
- Immediate partial top-up: $75,000 (invoiced upon signature)
- Second tranche: $125,000 invoiced at co-term (2028-12-31)
- Onboarding credit: 3% of total uplift applied as a smoothing credit (3% of $200,000 = $6,000) — applied across the first 3 months after signature to reduce early OPEX impact.
- Co-term: Aligns entire contract to 2028-12-31; if Reverie agrees to a 12-month renewal at co-term we can escalate to a 5% onboarding credit (requires sales leadership sign-off).
- Legal: Attached editable SOW (Word) with staged top-up and pro-rata invoicing language; key points called out in-line for your counsel.

Attachments: Reverb_Renewal_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF preview) and editable Word SOW & pricing matrix included via Hub link / DocuSign option: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/RWI-0447 (for signature).

Request: Please confirm if the staged path + 3% credit is acceptable by Friday EOD so we can issue the initial invoice and get procurement approval queued. If you’d like a short call to walk the spread, Lauren and I are available Friday 10–11am PT.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Best,
Ben
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
